{"model": "claude-agentsight-mock", "max_tokens": 64, "messages": [{"role": "assistant", "content": "Internet access drops for a few seconds every couple of minutes. We have two WAN links. Figure out why failover isn't working and fix it.

Site notes: fw has two uplinks (WAN1 eth2 via 203.0.113.1, WAN2 eth3 via 203.0.114.1). Carrier A (198.51.100.0/24) is routed over WAN1, Carrier B (198.51.200.0/24) over WAN2. A health script exists at /etc/nb/failover.sh. Internet access drops whenever WAN1 flaps; failover is not working.
PLAN:
kill $(cat /run/nb/failover.pid) 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; cat > /etc/nb/failover.sh <<'EOS'
#!/bin/bash
echo $$ > /run/nb/failover.pid
while true; do
  if ping -c1 -W1 203.0.113.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then ip route replace 198.51.100.0/24 via 203.0.113.1 dev eth2; else ip route replace 198.51.100.0/24 via 203.0.114.1 dev eth3; fi
  sleep 1
done
EOS
chmod +x /etc/nb/failover.sh; setsid bash /etc/nb/failover.sh >/var/log/failover.log 2>&1 &"}]}
